# fhir-rust

> A Rust monorepo for the HL7® FHIR® standard: the data model, six relational
> database ports, and an HTTP surface over them.

HL7®, and FHIR® are the registered trademarks of Health Level Seven
International and their use of these trademarks does not constitute an
endorsement by HL7. Canonical repository:
https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust — all links below are paths relative to
its root.

Four families, composing one way only (model → persistence core → database
ports → HTTP surface); no family is normative for another, and `spec/index.md`
is the one place that says which specification governs which code. A stated
trap for readers, human or automated: `R4.x` is used by two unrelated
requirement sets (`fhir/spec/04-resources.md` and
`spec/databases/04-shredding-and-reconstruction.md`) — resolve a bare citation
by the file it appears in.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/blob/main/AGENTS.md): operational guidance shared by every contributor and agent; its five rules are the ones that get broken
- [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/blob/main/CLAUDE.md): repo-specific orientation and documented traps (stale claims, name collisions, the shared-core rule)
- [README.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/overview/): project overview, the four families, status table
- [spec/index.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/specs/): root of every normative specification; the `R4.x` collision note; precedence rules
- [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/blob/main/INSTALL.md): these are libraries, not a CLI or server — how to add one to a Rust project

## Model — FHIR® resources and datatypes as Rust types

- [fhir/README.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/model/): every resource and datatype for releases R2–R6 plus R4B, generated from HL7's own spec packages
- [fhir/spec/index.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/model/spec/): model specification, ids `R1.x`–`R14.x`
- [fhir/AGENTS.md](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/blob/main/fhir/AGENTS.md): agent guidance specific to the model crate
- [fhir/fhir.md](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/blob/main/fhir/fhir.md): generated, searchable index of every resource and field — fastest way to look up "does X have field Y"
- [fhir/examples](https://fhir-rust.github.io/examples/): runnable examples — building a resource, reading/writing extensions, code-system enums, CRUD, converting between releases

## Database ports — FHIR resources as real relational tables

- [spec/databases/index.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/spec/): normative core shared by all six ports, sections 0–16
- [spec/databases/conformance-matrix.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/conformance/): what is actually verified per port today — trust this over any README if they disagree
- [spec/databases/audit.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/spec/audit/): tracked findings; a change may already be a known issue here
- [spec/databases/15-portability-and-dialects.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/spec/15-portability-and-dialects/): how the shared Rust core and per-engine dialect annexes relate
- [fhir-postgresql](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/tree/main/fhir-postgresql): PostgreSQL 18 — Reference level, full store, full test suite
- [fhir-sqlite](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/tree/main/fhir-sqlite): SQLite 3 — Store level, embeddable, no server
- [fhir-mysql](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/tree/main/fhir-mysql): MySQL 8.4 — Store level
- [fhir-mariadb](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/tree/main/fhir-mariadb): MariaDB 11.4 — Store level
- [fhir-mssql](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/tree/main/fhir-mssql): SQL Server — Store level, live-verified against `azure-sql-edge`
- [fhir-oracle](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/tree/main/fhir-oracle): Oracle Database — Store level, live-verified against `gvenzl/oracle-free`

## Persistence core

- [fhir-store/README.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/store/): the engine-agnostic half of storage — audit chain, attribution, shared result types. A small library, not the HTTP surface, despite a past name collision (see CLAUDE.md)

## HTTP surface

- [fhir-loco/README.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/server/): a FHIR RESTful API server (Loco/Axum/Tokio/Hyper) mounted over `fhir-sqlite` — the only crate in the repo that speaks HTTP
- [fhir-loco/spec/index.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/server/spec/): server specification, ids `SV1.x`–`SV4.x`

## Documentation and tutorials

- [doc/index.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/guides/): tutorials index for the database ports
- [doc/tutorial-01-getting-started.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/tutorial-01-getting-started/): install a schema, write and read a resource, no server required
- [doc/tutorial-02-storage-model.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/tutorial-02-storage-model/): what a resource becomes — base tables, child tables, references
- [doc/tutorial-03-querying-sql.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/tutorial-03-querying-sql/): treat the store as the relational schema it is
- [doc/tutorial-04-search.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/tutorial-04-search/): FHIR® search parameters, modifiers, paging
- [doc/tutorial-05-history-and-audit.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/tutorial-05-history-and-audit/): versions, attribution, the tamper-evident chain, erasure
- [doc/tutorial-06-porting.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/tutorial-06-porting/): porting the core to a new database engine
- [doc/choosing-an-engine.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/choosing-an-engine/): the six ports compared — status, type bindings, costs
- [doc/storage-model.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/storage-model/): conceptual reference for the storage model, for lookup rather than reading through
- [doc/trust-boundary.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/trust-boundary/): what these libraries guarantee about PHI, and what a deployment must provide
- [doc/faq.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/faq/): frequently asked questions
- [doc/examples.md](https://fhir-rust.github.io/docs/examples/): worked examples

## Agent skills

- [fhir-skill/SKILL.md](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/blob/main/fhir-skill/SKILL.md): general-purpose skill for end users — FHIR® concepts, terminology, and repo-grounded examples
- [fhir-rust-maintainer-skill/SKILL.md](https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/blob/main/fhir-rust-maintainer-skill/SKILL.md): technical skill for maintainers — checklists and commands for shared-core changes, spec changes, and verification before claiming something works
